title: Polynomial-time verifier fields
statement: For every bit string $z$, each of the following functions is polynomial-time computable: its code field, input field, unary width field, unary clock field, and certificate component, as obtained by the total parsing and projection operations defining these fields; and the function returning the one-bit word encoding whether the specified parsing and unary-field validity checks all hold.
replaced: For a bit string $z$, write $s(z)$ for its odd split (the self-delimiting pair encoding $\langle z_{[:i]}, z_{[i:]}\rangle$ when $|z| = 2i+1$, and the empty word when $|z|$ is even), $\pi_1, \pi_2$ for the two components of a pair encoding (the empty word when parsing fails), $Y = \pi_1(s(z))$ and $W = \pi_2(s(z))$; the code, input, width and clock fields of $z$ are $\pi_1(Y)$, $\pi_1(\pi_2(Y))$, $\pi_1(\pi_2(\pi_2(Y)))$ and $\pi_2(\pi_2(\pi_2(Y)))$. The guard $G(z)$ holds when $s(z)$, $Y$, $\pi_2(Y)$ and $\pi_2(\pi_2(Y))$ all parse as pair encodings and the width and clock fields consist only of ones. Then the maps sending $z$ to its code field, input field, width field, clock field and to $W$, and the map sending $z$ to the single bit $G(z)$, are all polynomial-time computable.
